cards.title: Bayesian NCA for Serial Sacrifice Designs
cards.claim: A Bayesian approach using MCMC (BUGS) can estimate the posterior distribution of AUC0-∞, tissue-to-plasma AUC ratios, and Drug Targeting Index (DTI) in serial sacrifice designs, providing valid uncertainty estimates (credible intervals) where frequentist methods (Bailer, Yuan) fail to account for within-animal plasma-tissue correlation or underestimate variance.
conditions: Study design must be serial sacrifice (destructive sampling) with sparse data (one sample per animal).
Non-informative (vague) priors are used unless prior knowledge is available.
Within-animal correlation between plasma and tissue concentrations is modeled via a bivariate normal likelihood.
required_inputs: Concentration data (plasma and tissue) at discrete time points.
Assumption of log-normality for concentration data.
Definition of terminal phase (e.g., last 3 time points) for λz estimation.
limitations: Requires Bayesian statistical expertise and MCMC software (e.g., OpenBUGS).
Prior specification is subjective, though vague priors minimize this.
Assumes linear distributional kinetics (no saturation of efflux transporters in the model structure, though inference on ratios remains valid).
Does not replace compartmental modeling for mechanistic insight but improves NCA parameter uncertainty.
cards.downstream_use: Statistical comparison of tissue penetration (partition coefficients) between genotypes or formulations in preclinical PK studies; quantifying uncertainty in exposure metrics derived from destructive sampling.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
